profile.reading:
Csquare IAD1-B sits at 45845 Nokes Boulevard, Sterling, Virginia 20166, one of three buildings, IAD1-A, IAD1-B, and IAD1-C, on Csquare's IAD1 campus in Loudoun County's Northern Virginia data center corridor. Csquare, formerly branded Centersquare, was launched in April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, with Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business held by Brookfield since 2019. Csquare went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists IAD1-B individually at 37,878 square feet sellable and 49.6 percent leased as of March 31, 2026. Csquare's public spec sheet gives only a combined campus total across all three IAD1 buildings, 141,621 square feet of raised floor, 143.2 megawatts of utility power, 19.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 37.5 megawatts of generator capacity, with chilled-water cooling and SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, ISO 27001, and ENERGY STAR certifications applying campus-wide rather than broken out per building. All three IAD1 buildings are leased rather than Csquare-owned, per the SEC filing. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date for IAD1-B. Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County as a matter of public record, and the county's data center corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing operators within a few miles of the IAD1 campus.

Csquare's Sterling, Virginia IAD1 campus sits within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, alongside dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and the same filing notes the company's legal predecessor entity, BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, was formed in May 2018 as a Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III vehicle, well before the 2024 Cyxtera and Evoque combination that produced the assets tracked in this dataset. Among the three IAD1 buildings, IAD1-B is the smallest by the SEC's per-building sellable square footage and IAD1-C the largest, a spread the campus-wide spec sheet totals do not surface. Because IAD1's three buildings, IAD2's two pods, and IAD4's two buildings are separate physical campuses several miles apart in different unincorporated communities within Loudoun County (Sterling for IAD1 and IAD2, Ashburn for IAD4), none of Csquare's campus-wide power or floor-space figures should be attributed to any single building in this dataset without the qualification that the number covers the whole named campus.

reading.body:
Centersquare IAD1-B is one of three buildings on the IAD1 campus in Sterling, Virginia, a complex sharing 141.2 megawatts of utility power, 19.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 37.5 megawatts of generator capacity across 141,621 square feet of raised floor. The campus sits in Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the world's largest concentration of data center capacity, where dozens of competing operators within miles share access to Dominion Energy's grid. IAD1-B itself measures 37,878 square feet of sellable space and was 49.6 percent leased as of March 2026, making it the smallest of the three IAD1 buildings by published floor area.

The published power and generator figures apply to the entire three-building IAD1 campus, not to IAD1-B alone, so no single-building capacity can be stated from the operator's spec sheet. If IT load at IAD1 scales to 40 kilowatts per rack, a common density for AI training, the campus's 143.2 megawatts of utility power could serve roughly 3,600 racks; at 50 kilowatts per rack, roughly 2,900 racks. The campus holds SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, ISO 27001, and ENERGY STAR certifications, qualifying it for regulated workloads including national security and financial systems.

Centersquare's Virginia portfolio ranks 26th by published megawatts among all operators in the state, with IAD1 representing one of 25 facilities statewide disclosing power capacity. Virginia's mapped data center footprint spans 330 facilities total, but only this small sample publish technical specifications, leaving IAD1-B's actual position within the state and its share of regional AI build-out unquantified by public data.
